title: Common Array Operations
summary: Combine essential operations: calculating sums, decimal averages, finding min/max, counting occurrences, and linear search.
learningOutcomes: Implement accumulator patterns for sums and averages without truncation
Find minimum and maximum elements without 0-initialization bugs
Perform linear search returning matching index or -1

activities.title: Core Mechanics: Common Array Operations

breakdown.whatIsIt: Comprehensive exploration of Common Array Operations in Java.
breakdown.whyItMatters: Arrays provide high-performance, contiguous in-memory storage essential for real-world software engineering.
howItWorks: Accumulates elements into a running sum variable.
Compares candidate elements against running minimum and maximum.
Scans sequentially from index 0 to length - 1 for target matches.
Exits early upon finding matches to achieve best-case performance.
keyTakeaways: Initialize min and max to arr[0] to support negative sets.
Cast sum to double for decimal accuracy.
Linear search inspects elements in O(N) time and returns -1 if missing.
Guard against empty arrays (arr.length == 0) to avoid division by zero.

activities.title: Verified Java Implementation: Reusable Array Operations Suite
activities.description: Demonstrates modular static methods for findMax, calculateAverage, and linearSearch tested on student scores.

steps.explanation: findMax initializes max = arr[0] and updates whenever arr[i] > max.
calculateAverage sums values and casts (double) sum / arr.length.
linearSearch returns matching index or -1 if absent.
main() tests all three methods with realistic student scores.

questions.prompt: Why should 'int max' be initialized to 'arr[0]' instead of 0 when finding the maximum element?
options: If the array contains only negative numbers, initializing max to 0 produces an incorrect answer of 0
Because Java prohibits setting max to 0
It doesn't matter; both always work
questions.explanation: If all numbers are negative (e.g. {-10, -5, -20}), 0 is greater than all elements and would be incorrectly returned as the maximum.

questions.prompt: What is the standard sentinel return value in Java search methods to indicate that a target was not found?
questions.explanation: Since 0 is a valid array index, search algorithms return -1 to unambiguously indicate that the target is not present in the array.

questions.prompt: Why is casting '(double) sum / arr.length' necessary when computing the average of integer array elements?
options: Without casting, Java performs integer division which truncates the decimal remainder (e.g. 7 / 2 becomes 3 instead of 3.5)
Without casting, the compiler raises a syntax error
Because average cannot be stored in double
questions.explanation: Dividing two integers in Java results in integer division, discarding fractions. Casting at least one operand to double preserves decimal accuracy.

questions.prompt: What is the worst-case time complexity of Linear Search on an unsorted array of size N?
questions.explanation: In the worst case (target at the very end or absent), Linear Search must inspect all N elements, giving O(N) linear time complexity.

questions.prompt: What happens if findMax() is called with an empty array of length 0 using 'int max = arr[0];'?
options: Throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException because index 0 does not exist
questions.explanation: In an empty array of length 0, accessing arr[0] throws an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Production code should validate array length first.

questions.prompt: In Linear Search, why should you return immediately upon finding a match rather than continuing to loop?
options: To avoid unnecessary comparisons and achieve best-case O(1) performance
Because Java loops can only run once
Because continuing would reverse the array
questions.explanation: Early returns terminate the method as soon as the target is found, saving CPU cycles.

questions.prompt: Given: 'int[] a = {12, 45, 7, 88, 32};'. What is the value of min after correct execution of findMin?
questions.explanation: The smallest value in the array is 7.

questions.prompt: How many comparisons does Linear Search make if the target element is at index 0?
questions.explanation: If the target is at index 0, the first comparison succeeds and returns immediately, achieving best-case O(1) time.

practice.title: Calculate Integer Array Sum
practice.problemStatement: Write a static method 'calculateSum(int[] arr)' that computes and returns the sum of all elements. In main(), test with {10, 20, 30, 40} and print 'Sum: 100'.

interviewQA.question: How do you find the maximum and minimum elements in an array in a single traversal?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Initialize both min and max to the first element (arr[0]). Iterate from index 1 to arr.length - 1. On each iteration, check if arr[i] < min and update min, and check if arr[i] > max and update max. This finds both in $O(N)$ time with at most $2N$ comparisons.
keyPoints: Emphasize memory layout, time complexity, and edge cases.

interviewQA.question: Why is -1 commonly returned in search algorithms when a target is not found?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Array indices are non-negative integers (0, 1, 2, ...). Returning any non-negative number like 0 could be misinterpreted as finding the item at index 0. Therefore, -1 serves as an unambiguous sentinel value indicating absence.
keyPoints: Emphasize memory layout, time complexity, and edge cases.

interviewQA.question: What is the danger of computing the sum of an integer array?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Integer overflow! If the array contains many large integers, their sum may exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE (2,147,483,647) and wrap around to negative numbers. To prevent this, accumulate the sum into a 'long' variable: 'long sum = 0;'.
keyPoints: Emphasize memory layout, time complexity, and edge cases.

interviewQA.question: How does Linear Search compare with Binary Search on arrays?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Linear Search works on any array (sorted or unsorted) in $O(N)$ time by inspecting elements sequentially. Binary Search requires the array to be sorted upfront, but eliminates half the remaining elements on each comparison, running in much faster $O(\log N)$ logarithmic time.
keyPoints: Emphasize memory layout, time complexity, and edge cases.

interviewQA.question: How do you handle calculating the average of an array if the array is empty (arr.length == 0)?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: You must include a guard clause: 'if (arr.length == 0) return 0.0;'. Dividing by 0 with floating-point numbers in Java produces Double.NaN (Not a Number), while integer division by 0 throws ArithmeticException.
keyPoints: Emphasize memory layout, time complexity, and edge cases.

interviewQA.question: What is the Two-Pointer technique often used in array algorithms?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: The two-pointer technique uses two integer index variables (e.g. left = 0 and right = arr.length - 1) that converge toward each other or move in tandem. It is used for in-place array reversal, palindrome checking, and pair sum problems in $O(N)$ time.
keyPoints: Emphasize memory layout, time complexity, and edge cases.

interviewQA.question: Can linear search be implemented recursively?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Yes. The base cases are: 1) if index >= arr.length return -1 (not found), 2) if arr[index] == target return index (found). Otherwise, return linearSearch(arr, target, index + 1). However, iterative linear search is preferred in Java to avoid Call Stack frame overhead.
keyPoints: Emphasize memory layout, time complexity, and edge cases.

activities.title: Self-Mastery Checklist
checklist: Accumulator Pattern: Initialize sum = 0 and accumulate each element across the loop.
Double Casting for Average: Cast sum to double: (double) sum / arr.length to prevent integer truncation.
Min/Max Initialization: Always initialize min and max to arr[0] (never 0) to support negative numbers.
Sentinel -1: Linear search returns -1 when target is absent; index >= 0 when found.
Early Return Optimization: Return immediately upon finding a match in search loops to save CPU cycles.
